status: Two fresh research additions and two workflow updates. Original weekly selections retained. All four new visual ideas are proposed, not implemented.
recommendation: Hexels paired with independent footprint and spatial-color controls is the strongest next advanced graphic. ReferStream is the strongest streaming-filmmaking research hook.

papers.title: ReferStream: introduce a subject without overwriting the whole scene.
papers.full_title: ReferStream: Interactive Subject Injection for Streaming Video Generation
papers.change: New post-cutoff paper on adding visual references during streaming generation without retraining or changing emitted frames.
papers.summary: Joint Latent extracts references in the current scene's context. Cache Restoration temporarily writes protected global KV slots for the arrival chunk, then restores them while retaining new generated history. Restoration is not stream rollback.
papers.evaluation: Author-run ReferStream Bench contains 68 curated entries: 48 InShot and 20 MultiShot. Overall New-ID similarity is 52.86 versus 39.99 for LongLive2; Existing-ID 73.18 versus 42.29; count accuracy 82.33% versus 73.90%. Similarity scores are scaled values, not recognition percentages.
papers.caveat: The collection was used during development; main results reuse archived outputs. LongLive2 gets no visual references; offline comparators get all references and the script upfront. Detection-based metrics lack human validation. Reference backgrounds can leak through rectangular placements, which do not guarantee final position. Cache restoration does not guarantee identity preservation. No independent reproduction.
papers.access: Public paper and 24 recorded examples. Official GitHub README/file tree explicitly contains a static project website and media; no runnable inference implementation or released benchmark package verified. Do not describe the GitHub link as released model code.
papers.creator_implication: A useful research direction for introducing props or characters after a shot has started. It is not yet a verified production tool or a real-time performance guarantee.
papers.visual_angle: Proposed original cache-state diagram: colored global, shot and local history slots; snapshot, inject, generate and restore. Move the arrival time and inspect which old entries return while new history remains. This would demonstrate state management, not generate video or predict identity scores.
papers.review_depth: Full methods, benchmark/evaluation limitations and ablations, official project and repository contents; no model execution.

papers.title: Hexels: one surface patch can hold a color gradient.
papers.full_title: Honeycomb-Surfels: Compact Hexagonal Primitives for Efficient Scene Rendering and Reconstruction
papers.change: New post-cutoff paper with an inspectable implementation of hexagonal surface primitives and a linked paper-model collection.
papers.summary: Combines soft hexagonal support with a first-order spatial color field, allowing a larger planar patch to represent smooth appearance changes. This is a splatting alternative for neural rendering/reconstruction, not generative 3D.
papers.evaluation: Authors evaluate 34 scenes: nine Mip-NeRF360, 15 DTU and ten Tanks and Temples, holding out every eighth camera. At matched uncompressed learned-model memory, reported PSNR gains over 2DGS range 4.53–7.38 dB across datasets. The separately reported 2.31× FPS gain uses primitive-matched comparisons; do not combine the two conditions.
papers.caveat: Matched model memory excludes optimizer state and does not mean equal training VRAM. Geometry and color representation change together. Fine texture, curvature, grazing angles and sparse initialization remain difficult; exported surface cells are not necessarily watertight. Native unconstrained baselines can win individual metrics. No independent reproduction.
papers.access: Trainer, CUDA kernel/viewer submodules and evaluation instructions verified. GitHub links jhu-ccvl/Hexels checkpoints; the Hub connector verifies that repository's metadata, but checkpoint files were not downloaded or evaluated. README specifies Linux/Python3.11/PyTorch2.5.1/CUDA12.x and testing on a 24GB RTX A5000; 24GB is tested capacity, not a universal minimum. Original code is MIT; inherited dependencies retain their own terms, including research/noncommercial restrictions. Hub metadata says license:other.
papers.creator_implication: Worth inspecting for compact captured-scene rendering and browser-viewable assets. The useful question is what each primitive can represent per byte, rather than whether hexagons always beat Gaussians.
papers.visual_angle: Proposed original analytic splatting lab: independently toggle Gaussian/hexagonal support and constant/linear color on a synthetic colored surface. Adjust primitive budget, boundary softness, texture frequency, curvature and camera angle; show residuals and overdraw separately from model bytes. Not a paper reproduction.
papers.review_depth: Full paper methods, dataset/budget/timing protocols, limitations, official code/readme and Hub metadata; no install or execution.

visual_queue.title: Give a new subject temporary access to the scene's memory.
visual_queue.idea: Animate a cache timeline showing temporary reference injection followed by restoration of protected global entries while new history remains.
visual_queue.controls: Arrival chunk; reference placement; restore toggle; global/local cache visibility; local history window; planned PNG/GIF.
visual_queue.misconception: Restoring the old cache deletes the new subject, or restoring a few entries guarantees that every future frame preserves identity.
visual_queue.connection: ReferStream, 27 Oct 2026. Proposed analytic state-machine explanation, not learned inference or an empirical quality predictor.
visual_queue.recommendation: Strong current filmmaking hook. Keep separate the guaranteed cache operation and the empirically uncertain visual outcome.

visual_queue.title: A splat can describe a gradient, not just one color.
visual_queue.idea: Render the same analytic surface with Gaussian or hexagonal footprints and constant or linear color, revealing where larger patches succeed and fail.
visual_queue.controls: Independent footprint/color toggles; patch count; edge softness; texture frequency; curvature; grazing camera; error/overdraw overlays; planned PNG/GIF.
visual_queue.misconception: The shape alone explains every improvement, or matching primitive count also matches bytes and training memory.
visual_queue.connection: Honeycomb-Surfels/Hexels, 27 Oct 2026. Synthetic rendering mechanism rather than trained scenes or benchmark reproduction.
visual_queue.recommendation: Best advanced colored graphic from today's papers; vary geometry and appearance independently.

visual_queue.title: More generated ads do not establish causal uplift.
visual_queue.idea: Show a creative feedback loop with separate review, paused-publication and activation gates, then compare biased selection with a randomized holdout.
visual_queue.controls: Variant count; traffic allocation; selection bias; review gate; activation gate; assumed conversion rates.
visual_queue.misconception: A higher volume of generated variants proves better marketing outcomes or automatically controls campaigns.
visual_queue.connection: Runway Ads GA, 27 Oct 2026. Proposed synthetic workflow and statistical illustration, not measured product performance.
visual_queue.recommendation: Useful competitor explainer; secondary to the rendering mechanism.

visual_queue.title: The video finished, but its audio timeline did not.
visual_queue.idea: Align frame and audio-sample grids; shorten the soundtrack and reveal the final assembly boundary, then pad with silence.
visual_queue.controls: Frame rate; frame count; audio sample rate; soundtrack end; floor/ceil duration; padding toggle.
visual_queue.misconception: Successful frame generation guarantees that final video/audio assembly will succeed.
visual_queue.connection: Openjutsu companion-pack audio fix, 28 Oct 2026. Proposed analytic timeline; no model inference.
visual_queue.recommendation: Small practical lesson about discrete time and pipeline failures.

workflow_changes.title: Openjutsu fixes missing source-slice node, slow setup checks and audio-shorter-than-video assembly failures
workflow_changes.classification: Useful local filmmaking workflow reliability update; not a new model or quality benchmark
workflow_changes.discovery_date: 2026-10-27; exact post UTC time not verified

primary_sources.change: Introduces H3SourceSlice; required source-frame/audio node was absent from the published Context-Loop dependency.
Replaces unpublished MiniMaxH3ContexLoopSourceSlice with H3SourceSlice in setup checks and Simple, Advanced, Montage and Object workflows.
Queries only required node definitions instead of the complete /object_info registry; fixes misleading connection/setup errors when large installs exceeded the eight-second timeout.
Pads audio to ceil(loaded video duration × sample rate), preventing final Chain Assemble failures when audio ends before video and rounding-related short silent tracks. Diff inspected.
Documents local H3/SAM/Qwen character and object editing, substantial setup requirements, model-dependent results, reflection failures and separate model/face-refinement licenses.

workflow_changes.date_scope: All listed commit timestamps lie inside the review window, with author and committer dates matching. Public push/visibility times were not independently established. The underlying project and workflows predate this window.
workflow_changes.evidence: Commit patches verify the setup and audio-padding changes. Reddit includes an independent setup-failure report followed by a report that the node fix worked, but no controlled evaluation or independent quality benchmark.
workflow_changes.creator_implication: If evaluating Openjutsu, update both the UI and companion swap pack before spending GPU time on long edits; an audio-duration mismatch could otherwise fail only after rendering.
limitations: Research/discovery only: nothing was installed or executed, and fixes were not runtime-tested here.
The author and users still report identity likeness and model inconsistency; reflections can leak the original appearance, and automatic role matching can fail.
One Reddit report says the setup fix worked; this is an anecdote, not proof of all-platform compatibility.
MIT app code does not cover all model/companion licenses. Face-refinement dependencies have additional restrictions.
Default DMAD/SolarRenderer workflow settings differ from the user's MiniMax H3 Turbo 8 preference. Do not install or run those defaults as an automatic fallback.
workflow_changes.visual_teaching_angle: A synchronized video/audio timeline: drag the audio end earlier than the final frame, display the discrete H3 clip grid, and toggle silence padding to explain why generation can finish while assembly fails. A separate mask/reference toggle can illustrate motion transfer versus identity leakage.
